correctness.rationale: Algebraic closure formula follows from idempotents plus normalized cycle-gain cosets. Uniform independent edge labels make each component cycle-gain map a uniform finite-field matrix, giving exact rank probabilities and size distribution. At sparse connectivity scale, mixed factorial/characteristic moments yield two isolated-count Poisson limits independent of normalized edge count, and a spanning-tree union bound excludes other components; finite-field surjectivity fails or holds with probability tending to one off the Gaussian threshold boundary. The resulting product probability is proved for every fixed p, c, t. The included direct-product enumerator checks seven full finite configurations including 2, 3 and 5 and both disconnected and complete supports; no finite sample is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The novel assertion under review is the two-parameter sparse-support/growing-vector-group critical limit exp(-2exp(-c))[1-Phi(t)]. Howie and Graham already solve the deterministic idempotent-generation criterion; Houghton already encodes edge labels as a map from cycle space. The present argument combines, and proves asymptotic independence of, an isolated-vertex Poisson limit and the total-edge Gaussian fluctuation to determine a joint threshold not stated in inspected source conclusions. Source and index searches found no statement with these equivalent parameters. The possibility of a broader random gain-graph theorem is explicitly unresolved.
residual_risks: A more general random voltage/gain-graph group-generation threshold might specialize to this result under different terminology.

value.rationale: Idempotent generation is a canonical semigroup property. Its random realization has two distinct obstructions (support connectivity and maximal-subgroup cycle-span surjectivity), and the theorem identifies a natural critical scaling on which both remain nontrivial, with an explicit product of Poisson and Gaussian tails. The joint independence argument and its dimension tuning are substantive, not merely a known-table computation; the exact conditional distribution clarifies the mechanism.
